dem.es: al, a quien (relativo de dativo masculino y neutro)
dem.en: to whom (masculine and neutral dative relative)

texto: When the name is the indirect complement (to whom), the relative is **dem** (masculine and neutral), **der** (feminine) and **denen** (plural). Example: **Der Kollege, dem ich helfe, ist nett** (the partner I help is nice). **Die Frau, der ich das Buch gebe** (the woman I give the book to). Plural: **Die Leute, denen ich schreibe** (the people I write to).

The relative follows the gender and number of the name, but the case is marked by the verb of the relative prayer. So **dem** appears with a masculine name in dative, while **den** was the relative of accusative masculine.
The verb of the relative prayer goes to the end: **dem ich helfe**.

filas: die Frau, der ich das Buch gebe

frases.de: Der Nachbar, dem ich immer helfe, ist sehr höflich.
frases.es: El vecino al que siempre ayudo es muy educado.
frases.en: The neighbor I always help is very polite.

frases.de: Die Nachbarin, der du Blumen gibst, freut sich bestimmt.
frases.es: La vecina a la que das flores seguro que se alegra.
frases.en: The neighbor you give flowers to sure is happy.

frases.de: Ja, und die Leute, denen wir schreiben, sind auch nett.
frases.es: Sí, y la gente a la que escribimos también es amable.
frases.en: Yeah, and the people we wrote to are nice too.

bloques.pregunta: What relative is correct for «The woman I give the book to» (feminine, dative)?

opciones.explicacion: It is nominee or accusative feminine.

bloques.pregunta: What relative goes with a plural in dativa?

opciones.explicacion: It is plural of nominative or accusative.

bloques.frase: Der Kollege, dem ich helfe, ist nett.

opciones.texto: The partner I help is nice.
The partner, whom I helped, is nice.

bloques.frase: Die Frau, ___ ich das Buch gebe, ist nett.
Die Leute, ___ ich schreibe, sind höflich.

bloques.pregunta: What does this statement say about the neighbor?
bloques.frase: Der Nachbar, dem ich helfe, ist höflich.

opciones.texto: The neighbor I give help to is educated and attentive.
opciones.explicacion: «dem ich helfe» is a relative sentence with verb that governs dative (helfen).

opciones.texto: The neighbor who helps me in the building is polite.
opciones.explicacion: In the German phrase the subject of the subordinate is «ich», not the neighbor.

opciones.texto: The neighbor I helped out last week was very polite.
opciones.explicacion: The original sentence is present as an indication («helfe», «ist»), not in preterito.

bloques.explicacion: the relative goes to the beginning and the verb to the end.

bloques.pregunta: What form of relative goes with «das Kind» (neutral) in dativa?

opciones.explicacion: It is nominative or neutral accusative.

bloques.pregunta: How exactly does «The neighbor I deliver flowers to» translate?

opciones.texto: die Nachbarin, der ich Blumen gebe
opciones.explicacion: «die Nachbarin» is antecedent feminine and «geben» requires indirect object in dative («der»).

opciones.texto: die Nachbarin, die ich Blumen gebe
opciones.explicacion: «die» would be an accuser or nominative, which would violate the «geben» dative regime.

opciones.texto: die Nachbarin, dem ich Blumen gebe
opciones.explicacion: «dem» is the dative mark for masculine and neutral genera, not feminine.

intro: Today we continue with the prayers of relative. You know the relative in nominative and accusative; now comes the **dativo**, and the relative with preposition.
